
'''Izumono Iwai Shrine''' (出雲乃伊波比神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located along the {{ill|Arakawa River (Kantō)|en|Arakawa River (Kantō)|qid=Q625465|lt=Arakawa River (Kantō)}} in {{ill|Akahama|ja|赤浜}}, {{ill|Yorii, Saitama|en|Yorii, Saitama|qid=Q961604|lt=Yorii}}, {{ill|Ōsato District, Saitama|en|Ōsato District, Saitama|qid=Q1075196|lt=Ōsato District}}, {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|qid=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}. It is one of the candidate sites for the {{ill|Izumo no Iwai Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|出雲乃伊波比神社 (曖昧さ回避)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 出雲乃伊波比神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q104539297}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳}} as a small shrine (式内小社) of {{ill|Musashi Province|en|Musashi Province|qid=Q907398|lt=Musashi Province}}’s {{ill|Obusuma district|ja|男衾郡|ko|오부스마군|qid=Q11578175}}. The former shrine Rank was that of a village shrine (郷社).

== History ==

Originally, the shrine was located in {{ill|Hatakeyama, Kawamoto Village|ja|川本村畠山}}. Due to the loss of ancient records in fires and floods, the exact founding date is unknown. During the {{ill|Former Nine Years' War|en|Former Nine Years' War|qid=Q1187448|lt=Zenkunen War}} (1052–1057) in the {{ill|Tengi|en|Tengi|qid=Q1193591|lt=Tenki era}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|en|Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|qid=Q3082851|lt=Minamoto no Yoriyoshi}} prayed for victory at this shrine while on his way to {{ill|Mutsu Province|ca|Província de Mutsu|cs|Provincie Mucu|de|Provinz Mutsu|es|Provincia de Mutsu|fa|ولایت موتسو|fi|Mutsun provinssi|fr|Province de Mutsu|gl|Provincia de Mutsu|id|Provinsi Mutsu|it|Mutsu (provincia)|ja|陸奥国|ko|무쓰국|lt|Mucu žemė|nl|Mutsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Mutsu|ru|Муцу (провинция)|simple|Mutsu Province|sk|Mucu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Муцу|tr|Mutsu (vilayet)|uk|Муцу (провінція)|zh|陸奧國|zh_classical|陸奧國|zh_min_nan|Mutu-kok|zh_yue|陸奧國|qid=Q907389|lt=Mutsu Province}} and dedicated a white flag. This event led to the shrine being renamed "Shirahata Hachiman Shrine" (白籏八幡社).

In {{ill|Kōji (Muromachi period)|en|Kōji (Muromachi period)|qid=Q1143910|lt=Kōji 3}} (1557), the shrine was relocated to {{ill|Shimogōchi, Akahama Village|ja|赤浜村下河内}}, known as "Hachimanzuka." Later, in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|en|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|qid=Q1145058|lt=Tenshō Era}} (1580), a major flood of the Arakawa River forced the shrine to move along with local residents to its current location.

In the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}, the shrine reverted to its original name, "Izumono Iwai Shrine."<ref name="Shrine Noticeboard">Shrine noticeboard (July 2019)</ref>

=== Enshrined Deities ===

* '''Main deity:''' {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|qid=Q272993}}
* '''Secondary deities:''' 
** {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命}}
** {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|qid=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ōjin}} (as {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|誉田別命|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 応神天皇|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q317997}})
** {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋根命|qid=Q2564508}}
** {{ill|Futodama|ja|天太玉命|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to フトダマ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11059539}}
** {{ill|Ame no Hohi|ja|天穂日命|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノホヒ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10940685}}

=== Shrine Rank ===

* '''November, Meiji 4 (1871):''' Promoted to village shrine (村社)
* '''June 24, Meiji 32 (1899):''' Promoted to district shrine (郷社)

== Festivals ==

* '''New Year's Festival (歳旦祭):''' January 1
* '''Setsubun Festival (節分祭):''' February 3
* '''Kinensai & Atago Festival (祈年祭・愛宕祭):''' February 23
* '''Prayers for New Students (入学児童祈願祭):''' Late March
* '''Yasaka Shrine Festival (末社八坂社祭):''' Mid-July (Sunday)
* '''Grand Festival (大祭):''' October 19
* '''Niinamesai & Atago Festival (新嘗祭・愛宕祭):''' October 23
* '''Onuki Festival (大抜祭):''' December 31
